entries.title: Multiplexed detector system precisely counts more than 9,000 photons
entries.summary: Researchers have developed a new approach that can precisely count from zero to more than 9,000 individual photons. The advance opens new possibilities for studying quantum light at large scales and making precise optical measurements.

entries.title: Chip-based laser cooling could ease quantum computing bottleneck
entries.summary: Researchers at Cornell have developed a laser-cooling technique that could potentially remove a significant bottleneck in the development of larger, faster quantum computers.

entries.title: Layered superionic conductor hosts atomic vibrations that behave like liquids, glasses and crystals
entries.summary: Scientists from the Institute of Metal Research (IMR) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have directly observed liquid-like, glass-like and crystal-like phonon behaviors coexisting in a crystalline solid—the layered superionic conductor AgCrSe₂.

entries.title: Research advances quantum computing that harnesses speed of light
entries.summary: Quantum computers have the potential to perform calculations more quickly than supercomputers, but they could be even faster and more energy-efficient if they were built with photons as their basic units, called qubits.
